    StartersPulled-closer half-moon pierogiBruce pulls the moon closer for Grace. Potato and cheddar pierogi, browned onion butter.How to make it300g plain flour, plus extra for rolling1 egg150g sour cream, plus extra to serve100g butter500g floury potatoes, peeled and chopped120g vintage cheddar, grated2 brown onions, 1 finely diced, 1 thinly sliced1 tbsp chives, snippedMix the flour, egg, 3 tbsp sour cream, 30g melted butter and half a teaspoon of salt into a soft dough, knead 3 minutes and rest under a bowl.Boil the potatoes until soft, mash with the cheddar, fry the diced onion in a little butter and stir it through. Season hard and cool.Roll the dough 2mm thick, cut 8cm rounds, fill each with a teaspoon of potato, fold into half moons and pinch the edges shut.Boil the pierogi in salted water until they float, then 1 minute more, and lift out.Fry the sliced onion in the rest of the butter until golden, add the pierogi and fry until crisp at the edges. Serve with sour cream and chives.Stanley Cup Buffalo wingsBruce makes the Sabres win the Cup. Hot sauce wings, blue cheese dip, celery.How to make it1.2kg chicken wings, tips off, split1 tbsp baking powder125ml Frank's RedHot sauce60g butter100g blue cheese, crumbled125g sour cream2 tbsp whole-egg mayonnaise1 lemon4 celery sticks, cut in batonsPat the wings dry and toss with the baking powder and a teaspoon of salt.Bake on a rack at 220°C, turning once, until crisp and golden.Mash the blue cheese into the sour cream, mayo and a squeeze of lemon.Melt the butter into the hot sauce and toss the wings through it.A jar of dill pickles on the counterBruce never touched his soup. Have a pickle.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.Blue PlatesRed Sea tomato soup and Grace's grilled cheeseBruce parts his tomato soup. Roast tomato soup, cheddar toastie on sourdough.How to make it1.6kg ripe tomatoes, halved1 brown onion, quartered5 garlic cloves3 tbsp olive oil700ml vegetable stock1 tsp brown sugar125ml thickened cream1 small bunch basil8 thick slices of sourdough200g vintage cheddar, grated100g mozzarella, grated50g soft butterToss the tomatoes, onion and garlic with the oil and salt and roast at 200°C until soft and blistered.Blend with the stock, sugar and half the basil, then simmer, stir in the cream and season.Fill the bread with both cheeses, butter the outsides and toast in a pan over medium heat until golden and melting.Ladle the soup into wide bowls, tear over the rest of the basil and serve each with a whole grilled cheese, cut corner to corner, for parting or dunking.The Pie CaseEvery prayer answered Yes sundaeBruce answers every prayer Yes. Every topping at once, under hot fudge.How to make it1 L vanilla ice cream150g dark chocolate, chopped150ml thickened cream2 tbsp golden syrup2 bananas, sliced250g strawberries, halved60g salted peanuts, chopped300ml whipped cream4 maraschino cherries2 tbsp rainbow sprinklesHeat the cream and golden syrup, pour over the chocolate and stir into a glossy fudge.Layer banana, strawberries and scoops of ice cream in 4 tall glasses.Pour over the hot fudge, then add the cream, peanuts, sprinkles and a cherry each.The FountainJuan Valdez iced coffeeBruce manifests himself some coffee.
